text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a classic public goods game where contributing tokens multiplies value for the group but keeping tokens is individually optimal—so while full cooperation maximizes total payoff, the dominant strategy is to free-ride and contribute zero. With 10 repeated rounds, I'm thinking about how this tension might play out over time.

I'll start with an opening move of contributing the full 20 to signal cooperative intent, planning to adjust with a tit-for-tat-style approach based on how others respond in later rounds. It's a bit risky, but opening cooperatively is a reasonable strategy here.
